headline: Enron says it will trade internet bandwidth; shares soar
text: At its annual analyst meeting on 20 January, Enron presented Enron Broadband Services, a high-speed network it says is run by software intelligence, and plans to trade network capacity the way it trades gas and power. Chairman Kenneth Lay cited a 700% return to shareholders over the decade. The shares rose by more than half in the month, to a record.
imageCaption: The Enron Building, 1400 Smith Street, Houston

headline: AOL, an internet company, agrees to buy Time Warner
text: On 10 January America Online, which brings more than 20 million customers onto the internet, announced that it will take over the media group Time Warner for about 165 billion dollars, paid in its own shares. Although Time Warner has far bigger revenues and assets, AOL's shareholders will own 55 percent of the combined company, because the stock market values AOL more highly. The deal shows how much buying power soaring internet shares have given their owners.
imageCaption: Steve Case (photograph from 2024)

headline: Rover's troubles deepen
text: Rover keeps losing money and market share in Britain. The pound has climbed above 3 marks, which makes Rover's British-built cars far more costly for BMW, and Rover's future is openly questioned in the British press, which puts off buyers. BMW is considering a strategic change of course.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 1999, preface by Joachim Milberg, https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_1999.pdf (read 2026-10-03); BBC News, 'Rover - a car firm's troubles', 29 October 1999, http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/353271.stm (read 2026-10-03); data/out/mercedes.json (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Rover 75, launched in 1998

headline: Ballmer replaces Gates as chief executive
text: Bill Gates handed the job of chief executive to Steve Ballmer, who joined Microsoft in 1980 and has been president since 1998. Gates stays chairman and becomes chief software architect.
imageCaption: Steve Ballmer, Microsoft's president
imageCredit: Martin Olsson (username 'mnemo' on en/sv wikipedia and commo

headline: New economy up, old economy down
text: The Nasdaq rose 19% in February to 4,697 while the S&P 500 of large established companies fell 2%. Chip, telecom and internet shares are bought, while old-economy favourites are sold: Nvidia rose 73% this month and Siemens 31%, while Coca-Cola and McDonald's fell about 15%. At the Super Bowl at the end of January, a record 17 dot-com companies advertised. About 248 million people were online at the end of 1999, fifteen times as many as four years earlier.
source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/NASDAQCOM (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble (read 2026-10-03); https://www.stackscale.com/blog/internet-evolution-statistics/ (search result read 2026-10-04); https://www.allaboutmarketresearch.com/internet.htm (search result read 2026-10-04) (figures of Internet World Stats)
imageCaption: Georgia Dome, 1996
imageCredit: MSGT Joseph Pittelli, U.S. Air Force

headline: Pets.com, the sock puppet company, goes public
text: Pets.com of San Francisco sold 7.5 million shares on the Nasdaq on February 11 at $11 each, raising $82.5 million. It sells pet food and supplies online and is famous for its sock-puppet mascot, which appeared in a Super Bowl advertisement in January. In its first year, to December 1999, it had sales of $5.8 million and a net loss of $61.8 million; Amazon.com owns about 30% of it.
imageCaption: The Pets.com sock puppet, microphone in paw, during the filming of a television commercial in Los Angeles, 11 January 2000

headline: Siemens profits double and the Infineon offer opens
text: On 24 January Siemens reported that first-quarter profit nearly doubled, raised its forecast and said all divisions were in the black; sales at Infineon rose more than 70%. From 21 February investors could subscribe for 25 to 30% of Infineon ahead of a listing in Frankfurt and New York on 13 March. Siemens shares rose 31% in February.
imageCaption: Infineon, Siemens' chip arm, at a trade fair stand

headline: Cisco becomes the world's most valuable company
text: On March 27 Cisco's stock market value reached about $555 billion, more than Microsoft's, making it the most valuable company in the world. The shares were split two-for-one on March 22, the ninth split since the 1990 listing. Investors value Cisco as the company whose equipment carries the internet.
source: https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/business-and-management/cisco-systems-goes-public (read 2026-10-03); split from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/0000891618-00-001722.txt (read 2026-10-03), count of splits from https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/r/newsroom/en/us/a/y1999/m05/cisco-systems-reports-third-quarter-earnings-and-two-for-one-stock-split.html (eighth split, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Aerial view of Cisco's San Jose campus under construction, May 1999
imageCredit: Cisco Systems (Center for Cisco Heritage archive, Computer History Museum)

headline: The Nasdaq tops 5,000 and the S&P 500 sets a record
text: The Nasdaq index closed at a record 5,048.62 on 10 March, and the S&P 500 rose 10% in March, closing above 1,500 for the first time on 22 March and setting a new record on 24 March. Fed officials worry that the high valuations of many technology shares could see a sizable correction, as the market grows more volatile.
imageCaption: A woman walks past the Nasdaq sign in Times Square, New York, on 9 March 2000, the day the Nasdaq Composite first closed above 5,000

headline: Investors ask how long the dot-coms' cash will last
text: On March 20 the financial weekly Barron's published a cover story warning that many internet companies are running out of cash fast. The Nasdaq index, which set a record on March 10, has fallen since.
imageCaption: Barron's cover of 20 March 2000, 'Burning Fast': dozens of internet companies are likely to run through their cash this year
imageCredit: Barron's cover (not credited on the page)

headline: Lehman's quarterly profit more than doubles
text: Lehman Brothers earned a record $541 million in the quarter to February, up 156% from a year earlier, on record revenues of $2.2 billion, driven by share underwriting and merger advice in the technology boom. 'The firm is clearly hitting on all cylinders,' said Richard Fuld.
imageCaption: The trading floor of the New York Stock Exchange

headline: Microsoft picks Nvidia for the Xbox
text: On 5 March Nvidia agreed with Microsoft to develop and sell the graphics processors for Microsoft's planned games console, the Xbox, which Bill Gates presented on 10 March. Microsoft will pay Nvidia 200 million dollars in advance against future chip purchases.
imageCaption: Bill Gates shows the Xbox

headline: BMW breaks up Rover and the shares jump
text: On 16 March BMW announced that it is giving up Rover. Rover Cars and the Longbridge plant go to the British investor Alchemy Partners, with BMW paying to be rid of them; Land Rover is to be sold to Ford, reportedly for 1.8 billion pounds. BMW keeps the Cowley plant near Oxford to build the new Mini. A one-off charge of 3.15 billion euros produced a net loss of 2.49 billion euros for 1999.
source: BBC News, 'BMW splits up Rover', 17 March 2000, http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/679169.stm (read 2026-10-03); BMW Group Annual Report 1999, https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_1999.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW (16 March 2000, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rover_Group (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Rover car plant at Longbridge, Birmingham, 1998

headline: The Nasdaq loses 25% in a week
text: On 3 April a judge ruled that Microsoft broke antitrust law; Microsoft fell 15% and the Nasdaq 8% that day. On 14 April the Nasdaq fell 9.7%, ending a week in which it lost 25%. It ended April at 3,861, almost a quarter below its March record.
imageCaption: An investor peers through a window at the Nasdaq board in Times Square while the news ticker reads 'Nasdaq continues its plunge', New York, 4 April 2000

headline: Judge rules Microsoft broke the antitrust law
text: On 3 April Judge Jackson ruled that Microsoft illegally monopolised the market for PC operating systems and illegally tied its browser to Windows. Microsoft's shares fell 15% that day and the Nasdaq index 8%, adding to the slide in technology shares that began in March.
imageCaption: Bill Gates during his videotaped deposition for the government's antitrust case against Microsoft, 27 August 1998

headline: 'Maybe the music has stopped': the Nasdaq is down a third
text: The slide of technology shares goes on. On 23 May the Nasdaq index fell as low as 3,173, 37 percent below its record of 5,049 on 10 March. A week earlier, on 16 May, the Fed had raised its interest rate by half a point to 6.5 percent to cool the economy. Even the most famous investors have been caught out. George Soros, whose Quantum Fund lost 19 percent this year on internet shares, said: 'Maybe I don't understand the market. Maybe the music has stopped, but people are still dancing.' His chief investor Stanley Druckenmiller resigned on 28 April: 'I overplayed my hand.' Julian Robertson, who refused to buy internet shares at all, had given up a month earlier and closed his Tiger funds.
source: https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2000/may/23/markets-have-wild-ride/ (search result read 2026-10-04); https://www.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/0005/16/bn.01.html (search result read 2026-10-04); https://money.cnn.com/2000/04/28/mutualfunds/soros/ (search result read 2026-10-04); https://www.safalniveshak.com/risks-of-speculating-during-rising-markets/ (search result read 2026-10-04); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Robertson (read 2026-10-04); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble (read 2026-10-04)
imageCaption: George Soros, photographed years later on a visit to the European Commission

headline: The 'I love you' virus
text: From 4 May an e-mail with the subject 'ILOVEYOU' spread around the world, first in Asia, then in Europe as people arrived at work, then in America. Its attachment, a computer worm, overwrites files and sends itself to everyone in the victim's address book. Companies shut down their e-mail systems. It was traced to the Philippines.
imageCaption: The 'ILOVEYOU' e-mail with its LOVE-LETTER attachment

headline: Pets.com sells at a loss
text: Pets.com reported sales of $7.7 million for the first quarter, against $12.5 million spent on the goods and shipping, and $28.9 million on marketing. The net loss was $39.1 million. The company said its gross margin improved from minus 124% to minus 64% after it opened a second warehouse in Indianapolis.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100683/000089161800002857/0000891618-00-002857.txt (10-Q for the quarter to March 31, 2000, filed May 15, 2000, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The sock puppet, a parrot and the clapperboard on the set of a Pets.com commercial, Los Angeles, January 2000

headline: Florida caps the Engle bond; Philip Morris eyes Nabisco: tobacco shares rally
text: In early May the Florida legislature passed a bill that spares cigarette makers most of the risk of having to post a bond worth billions of dollars to appeal a verdict in the Engle class action, which could have bankrupted them. Philip Morris is also reported to be the frontrunner in the bidding for Nabisco. Philip Morris shares gained about 19% in May; analysts say investors think the worst is behind the companies.
source: https://www.wired.com/2000/05/holy-smoke-tobacco-boosts-dow/ (Reuters report of 15 May 2000, read 2026-10-03); move from data/out/mo.json
imageCaption: Dade County Courthouse, Miami, Florida

headline: The court orders Microsoft split in two
text: On 7 June the court ordered Microsoft to submit within four months a plan to split into two companies, one for operating systems and one for applications, which may not merge or share technology for ten years. Microsoft is appealing.
imageCaption: The federal courthouse in Washington, where the Microsoft case was tried

headline: Amazon grows 84% but keeps losing money
text: On July 26 Amazon reported second-quarter sales of $578 million, up 84%, a pro forma operating loss of $89 million and $908 million of cash. The day before, it announced the resignation of its president. Investors have turned against loss-making internet companies.
imageCaption: Time's Person of the Year issue of 27 December 1999: Jeff Bezos in an Amazon shipping box, 'E-commerce is changing the way the world shops'

headline: Engle jury: 145 billion dollars in punitive damages
text: A Florida jury ordered Philip Morris and four other tobacco companies to pay 145 billion dollars in punitive damages to the class of sick Florida smokers, by far the largest award in US history. Philip Morris's share is nearly 74 billion dollars. The companies will appeal, and under the new Florida law the bond they must post is limited.
source: https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2001-feb-02-fi-20218-story.html (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Engle (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Florida (largest punitive award, read 2026-10-03); month change from data/out/mo.json
imageCaption: Stanley Rosenblatt (right), lawyer for the Engle class of Florida smokers, with plaintiffs Frank Amodeo, Ralph Della Vecchia and Mary Farnum, Miami

headline: Nokia warns, and the shares lose a quarter in a day
text: On 27 July Nokia reported record second-quarter profit, up 62%, but said third-quarter earnings per share will fall below the 0.20 euros just reported, before new internet-enabled phones take hold. Its ADR fell 26.5% in a day in New York.
imageCaption: The Nokia 3310, 2000

headline: Regulators kill the Sprint deal
text: WorldCom and Sprint called off their merger on 13 July after the U.S. Justice Department and the European Union said they would block it, arguing it would limit competition in long distance and put too much of the internet under one company.
imageCaption: Joel Klein (photograph from 2008)

headline: IBJ's last month: Mizuho Holdings takes over
text: The holding company Mizuho Holdings is to be created on 29 September through an exchange of shares of the three banks. August is the last month IBJ shares can be traded in the game; holders are paid out at the August price.
imageCaption: Offices of the new Mizuho group in Tokyo

headline: Pets.com says its cash will last only into early 2001
text: In its quarterly report filed on August 14 Pets.com said its cash should be enough only into the first quarter of 2001 and that it expects to have to raise more money then. It is still selling goods for less than they cost.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100683/000089161800004394/e10-q.txt (10-Q for the quarter to June 30, 2000, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pets.com (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Pets.com sock puppet, the company's advertising mascot

headline: Enron shares hit a record near $90
text: Enron's shares reached a record of about $90 on 23 August. Rebecca Mark, who built Enron's international power business and ran its water company Azurix, has left after a slump in Azurix's shares.
imageCaption: Enron's Code of Ethics booklet, July 2000

headline: GE is the most valuable company in the world
text: General Electric's stock market value has passed 600 billion dollars, making it the most valuable company in the world. A large part of that value rests on GE Capital, its lending, leasing and insurance arm.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric (read 2026-10-03, citing Boston Business Journal 2018-10-30: market value of $601 billion in August 2000); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Welch (read 2026-10-03, financial services share)
imageCaption: Jack Welch, chairman and chief executive of General Electric

headline: Apple's sales warning halves the shares
text: At the end of September Apple warned that sales for the quarter to September will fall well short of its expectations. The new G4 Cube computer, launched in July, is selling far below plan, education sales are weak, and buyers chose cheaper Power Macs; dealers are sitting on unsold computers. Apple expects sales to fall sharply in the next quarter as well.
imageCaption: The Power Mac G4 Cube, introduced in July 2000

headline: Intel warns, and loses a fifth in a day
text: On 21 September Intel said third-quarter revenue would grow only 3 to 5% from the second quarter, to 8.5 to 8.7 billion dollars, well short of what analysts expected, blaming weak sales in Europe. The shares fell 21% in after-hours trading, from 61.48 to 48.06 dollars, and kept falling; it was a record trading day for a US stock.
imageCaption: An Intel Pentium III processor

headline: Pets.com cuts costs and looks for a buyer
text: Pets.com opened a customer service centre in Greenwood, Indiana, and moved most of its customer staff there to cut costs. It is trying to raise capital or sell the company.
imageCaption: Sock puppet (photograph from 2008)

headline: Bush or Gore? America votes and has no winner
text: Americans voted on 7 November, and three weeks later they still do not know who their next president is. Everything hangs on Florida: on election night the television networks called the state for Al Gore, then for George W. Bush, then for nobody, and Gore phoned Bush to concede and took it back. Bush led by 1,784 votes on election night and by 327 after a machine recount; Gore asked for recounts by hand in four counties, where officials now study punch cards that voters did not punch through cleanly. On 26 November Florida declared Bush the winner by 537 votes, and Gore went to court the next day.
imageCaption: 2000 United States presidential election recount in Florida, 2000

headline: Pets.com shuts down
text: On November 7 Pets.com said it will stop taking orders on November 9, lay off 255 of its 320 employees and sell its inventory, warehouse equipment, web addresses and the sock-puppet brand. More than 50 possible buyers and investors were approached; none would fund or buy the company. The shares, issued at $11 in February, traded at about 19 cents, and the company warned that shareholders may receive little or nothing.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100683/0001095811-00-004383.txt (8-K with press release, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pets.com (read 2026-10-03); liquidation estimate from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100683/000109581100005560/f67985dsdefs14a.txt (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Pets.com home page announcing that the shop will stop taking orders on 9 November 2000

headline: The Nasdaq's worst month since 1987; Pets.com closes
text: The Nasdaq fell 23% in November to 2,598, half its March record and its worst month since October 1987. Pets.com announced on 9 November that it will shut down, nine months after its IPO. The sell-off has spread from internet start-ups to the big chip, PC and telecom equipment companies. Gloomy profit reports and signs of slower growth sent the S&P 500 down 8% in the month to 1,314.95.
imageCaption: Times Square (photograph from 2009)

headline: WorldCom splits itself in two and writes off $685 million
text: On 1 November WorldCom announced it would split its business into two tracking stocks: WorldCom group for data, internet and business customers, and MCI group for the shrinking consumer long-distance business, which will pay a dividend. It has taken a $685 million third-quarter charge for customers that cannot pay, as many small telecom companies go bankrupt, and its growth is slowing. A filing on 14 November disclosed that WorldCom had lent chief executive Bernard Ebbers money and guaranteed his loans so he would not have to sell shares to meet margin calls.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723527/000091205701505916/a2043540z10-k405.txt (WorldCom 10-K for 2000, describing the 1 November announcement and the third-quarter charge; read 2026-10-03); http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/money/industries/telecom/2002-11-05-ebbers-loans-timeline_x.htm (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Telephone line

headline: Enron denies rumours of a profit warning
text: Enron's president Jeffrey Skilling said on 24 November that rumours of a profit warning were untrue, adding that the company was very comfortable with analysts' forecasts of 35 cents a share for the fourth quarter and $1.65 for 2001. The shares fell about a fifth in November as the market slid and as Wall Street worried about California's power market, where a leading utility analyst suspended his ratings on energy companies in October.
imageCaption: Kenneth Lay, chairman of Enron, 1999

headline: Credit Suisse buys Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette
text: In November Credit Suisse completed its purchase of the US investment bank Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette for about $12.4 billion, to be merged into Credit Suisse First Boston.
imageCaption: Lukas Mühlemann, chief executive of Credit Suisse Group, speaking at the St. Gallen Management Symposium, 1996

headline: Cisco says it sees no slowdown
text: Cisco's sales are still growing fast, and in November its chief strategy officer said: 'We haven't seen any sign of a slowdown.' Some component suppliers have begun to lower their forecasts. Cisco's shares are down by about 40% from their March high.
imageCaption: Building 10 on Cisco's campus in San Jose, the company's head office

headline: UBS takes over PaineWebber
text: UBS completed its takeover of the US broker PaineWebber on 3 November for about $11.8 billion. PaineWebber has 1.9 million mostly affluent clients with $452 billion of assets. It makes UBS a big player in American wealth management.
imageCaption: The Paine Webber office in the early twentieth century

headline: The Supreme Court decides the election for Bush
text: Five weeks after the vote of 7 November, the US Supreme Court stopped the Florida recount on 12 December in Bush v. Gore, and Al Gore conceded the next day. George W. Bush won Florida by 537 votes and the electoral college by 271 to 266, while Gore won more votes nationwide.
imageCaption: United States Supreme Court Building

headline: Natural gas soars, California runs short of power
text: The US natural gas price at Henry Hub averaged $8.90 per million Btu in December, almost four times its level a year ago, while California's deregulated power market faces shortages and soaring prices. Crude meanwhile fell 20% in December to about $27 a barrel. Drillers and gas traders are the winners.
imageCaption: A dispatcher in the control room of California's grid operator takes the call for a stage two power emergency, Alhambra, 11 December 2000

headline: 2000 in review: the first losing year in a decade
text: The S&P 500 fell 10% in 2000 to 1,320.28, its first losing year since 1994 and its worst since 1977; the Dow lost 6.2%. Internet shares have collapsed: most are down 75% or more from their highs, and the dot-com crash has wiped out about 1.75 trillion dollars of value by November.
imageCaption: American shares (S&P 500) at the end of each month of 2000: down 10 percent in the year
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Yahoo Finance (^GSPC, month-end closes)

headline: Skilling to become Enron's chief executive
text: Enron's board elected Jeffrey Skilling chief executive from 12 February 2001, with Kenneth Lay remaining chairman; Skilling said Lay had put rumours of a move to Washington to rest. Enron had revenues of $40 billion in 1999 and $60 billion in the first nine months of 2000. It also agreed to buy back the public shares of its water company Azurix at $8.375 each.
imageCaption: Jeffrey Skilling, Kenneth Lay and Joseph Sutton of Enron, 1999 (left to right)

headline: Nvidia buys the assets of its old rival 3dfx
text: On 15 December Nvidia agreed to buy the technology and patents of 3dfx Interactive, the pioneer of 3D graphics cards for games in the mid-1990s, which has fallen behind.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/0001012870-01-500581.txt (Nvidia 8-K on the 3dfx asset purchase, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A 3dfx Voodoo5 5500 graphics card, 2000
